# CAS Handbook: How to Play
## Aerial Support & Deployment Platforms
This handbook explains the gameplay controls for fitting, loading, targeting, and firing dropship weapons. It is not an SOP, rules-of-engagement document, or UCMJ reference.
Dropships provide troop transport and Close Air Support (CAS). The available craft and attachment points depend on the map: examples include the [color=#D2B48C]Alamo[/color], [color=#808080]Normandy[/color], Fallujah, and Mohawk.
[bold]Both the [color=#D2B48C]Alamo[/color] and [color=#808080]Normandy[/color] are engineered to perform essential troop transport and devastating Close Air Support (CAS) missions[/bold], adapting to the dynamic needs of any operation.
This guide will cover the general aspects of troop transport, attachment overview and then provide a more in-depth look at executing effective Close Air Support.
## I. Troop Transport: Lifeline to the Front
Efficient troop transport is vital. While both dropships can ferry marines, the [color=#D2B48C]Alamo[/color] is often designated as the primary workhorse for shuttling squads and supplies between The Almayer and The Main LZ.
### Optimizing Your Transport Runs:
- [bold]Destination Selection:[/bold] Use the navigation console to select an available landing destination before launching. Transport travel and CAS fly-by runs are different flight modes. - [bold]Departure Callouts:[/bold] Be sure to announce departure times on [color=#808080]common ship radio[/color] to reduce the chance of leaving any marine behind on ship. - [bold]Have the Pilot Fly:[/bold] Having [color=#FFFF00]Piloting Skill 2[/color] (standard for Dropship/Gunship Pilots and ASOs) [color=#ADD8E6]reduces dropship refuel time by 25%[/color]. [bold]This stacks with the Cooling System.[/bold]
## II. Dropship Armaments & Engine Attachments
The CAS interface supports up to [bold]seven weapons[/bold], including weapons on internal points. This does not add attachment points to a craft: your actual loadout is limited by the exterior, engine, and interior points on its map. An interior weapon occupies a point that could otherwise hold a utility module.
### Preparing a Loadout
1. Print the weapon and its matching ammunition from the Dropship Part Fabricator. 2. Use a powerloader to move and install heavy weapon attachments on compatible points. 3. Load heavy GAU crates, laser batteries, and rocket packs with a powerloader. Match the ammunition to the installed weapon. 4. For BOFORS and Howitzer ammunition, take an individual magazine or shell from its tray or rack with [bold]both hands free[/bold], then click the weapon's attachment point to load it. Click the point with an empty hand to unload it. The whole tray or rack is a transport container, not the fired ammunition. 5. Open [bold]Equip[/bold] on the weapons console to check the installed weapon, loaded payload, and ammunition before flying.
Exterior powerloader loading is blocked while the dropship is in flight. Interior BOFORS and Howitzer mounts can be serviced by hand from the cabin; use them if you want to reload without returning to a landing pad.
### A. Weapon Systems
Exterior Bofors and Howitzer mounts on the Fallujah and Mohawk display the full weapon frame, whether loaded or empty. Interior mounts retain their separate loaded and unloaded artwork.
Interior-mounted Bofors, Howitzer, and JDAM bomb clamps are listed alongside exterior weapons. When more than four weapons are installed, use the [bold]PREVIOUS[/bold] and [bold]NEXT[/bold] buttons at the bottom of the equipment, strike weapon, or firemission editor screen to browse the weapon pages.
- [bold]Overview[/bold]: This is a powerful direct-fire cannon, offering versatility against a range of targets based on the ammunition selected. - [bold]Firing Window[/bold]: Usable during [color=#00FF00]Transit AND Fly-by runs[/color]. - [bold]Ammunition Types & Characteristics[/bold]:
[bold]General Description[/bold]: This round is designed for engaging [color=#FFA500]infantry, light vehicles, and unreinforced structures[/color]. It excels at area suppression and clearing out softer targets but is not intended for heavily armored threats. [color=#ADD8E6]Has a travel time of 10 seconds[/color]
[bold]General Description[/bold]: A specialized armor-piercing sabot round engineered to defeat [color=#FF6347]heavily armored targets[/color]. It is less effective against infantry or unarmored targets. [color=#ADD8E6]Has a travel time of 6 seconds[/color]
[bold]PGU-110 "Hornet"[/bold]: Wide dispersion, fragmentation damage, and small explosive impacts. Choose it for groups of exposed infantry; it has low armor penetration and cannot penetrate overhead cover.
[bold]PGU-115 "Lance"[/bold]: Narrow dispersion, high armor penetration, and up to three levels of overhead penetration. It uses focused direct damage rather than an explosive blast.
[bold]PGU-120 "Cinder"[/bold]: Scattered incendiary impacts for area denial, with reduced direct damage. It cannot penetrate overhead cover.
These GAU crates hold [bold]400 rounds[/bold] and spend [bold]40 rounds per trigger[/bold]: ten full bursts per crate. One trigger starts a burst, not a single bullet.
[bold]Building a mixed GAU belt[/bold]: 1. Print an empty mixed ammunition belt carrier. 2. With a powerloader, use a GAU crate on the carrier. Repeat for up to three crates; they fill slots 1, 2, and 3 in order. 3. Install the carrier in the GAU's ammunition point instead of a single crate. 4. Each trigger fires one whole burst from the next slot: 1, then 2, then 3, then back to 1. Empty slots and crates with fewer than 40 rounds are skipped. A full three-crate carrier supplies thirty bursts. 5. Examine the carrier to inspect the slot order. Use its slot eject verbs to remove crates and change the loadout.
Mixing does not blend damage types inside a burst. [bold]Next burst[/bold] in the console identifies the next crate's payload; [bold]Bursts left[/bold] counts usable bursts across the carrier. The same sequence is used by direct CAS triggers and fire missions. Different GAU ammunition types cannot refill one another, and a carrier cannot be refilled by combining it with another carrier.
- [bold]Overview[/bold]: An area denial weapon that projects a laser to create a field of intense, albeit short-lived fires. - [bold]Firing Window[/bold]: Can be used during [color=#00FF00]Transit AND Fly-by runs[/color]. - [bold]Ammunition & Characteristics[/bold]:
The cannon randomly covers a [color=#FFA500]7x7 area with 16 total fires[/color]. These fires have a very short duration but are of very high intensity, making them ideal for flushing enemies or temporary area denial. The ammunition is very cost-efficient, with a full reload providing 10 shots. It boasts the [color=#ADD8E6]fastest travel time of any CAS weapon (1 second)[/color] and has a minimal [color=#FFD700]1-tile inaccuracy[/color].
[bold]Green "Verdant"[/bold]: Wider green fire coverage; twenty triggers per battery.
[bold]Blue "Glacier"[/bold]: Concentrated blue fire coverage; five triggers per battery.
[bold]White "Daybreak"[/bold]: White-hot fire with a small footprint and high charge consumption; two triggers per battery.
[bold]Rapidfire[/bold]: Five simultaneous laser pulses per trigger, each igniting its own impact area. A full battery provides [bold]ten triggers[/bold], for fifty pulse impacts in total. It still uses the laser cannon's firing cooldown.
[bold]Changing the Rapidfire pattern[/bold]: Select the loaded laser cannon on either monitor, then click its pattern button to switch between [bold]Laser: wide ring[/bold] and [bold]Laser: sweeping line[/bold]. - [bold]Wide ring[/bold]: Five points around the aimpoint, six tiles from the center. There is no central pulse. - [bold]Sweeping line[/bold]: Five points across a twelve-tile line, including a central pulse. Both patterns follow the dropship's orientation and have the same charge cost. Check the preview before firing. Changing the pattern affects future shots, not pulses already released.
[bold]L/60 40mm BOFORS (ATC)[/bold]: Fits exterior weapon points and interior weapon-capable utility points. Each magazine holds twenty rounds; a trigger consumes five, providing [bold]four bursts per magazine[/bold]. All five ammunition types use genuine explosions, not GAU-style direct tile hits. - [bold]HE[/bold]: General explosive bombardment. - [bold]AP[/bold]: Penetrates cover before a focused explosive detonation. - [bold]Airburst[/bold]: Wider anti-infantry coverage, with selectable burst height. - [bold]HEAT[/bold]: A concentrated anti-armor explosive payload. - [bold]Incendiary[/bold]: Explosive impacts that also start fires.
[bold]Changing BOFORS airburst height[/bold]: Load an Airburst magazine, select the BOFORS on the console, and click the height button to cycle [bold]low, medium, and high[/bold]. Medium is the default. Low concentrates the blast into fewer tiles at higher intensity; high spreads the same explosive energy over more tiles at lower intensity. The preview updates with the setting.
These are detonation-height gameplay profiles above the target, [bold]not a selector for a building floor or z-level[/bold]. The setting is only available for BOFORS Airburst ammunition, requires the weapon's pilot skill, and affects future shots only.
[bold]M137 105mm Howitzer (HWR)[/bold]: Fits exterior and interior points and holds one physical shell at a time. Load a fresh shell after firing. - [bold]HE[/bold]: Heavy explosive damage against positions. - [bold]HE-FRAG[/bold]: Explosive fragmentation coverage. - [bold]HEAT[/bold]: Anti-armor bombardment. - [bold]HE Airburst[/bold]: Multiple dispersed explosive impacts from one physical shell. It does not use the BOFORS height selector.
[bold]JDAM Bomb Clamp (BMB)[/bold]: Fits interior crew-compartment points only and holds one JDAM-family bomb. Use a powerloader to install the clamp and load its matching bomb into the point. HE provides a large blast; Incendiary adds fire; AP emphasizes penetration; Cluster disperses bomblets; Napalm blankets an area in fire. A cluster payload's displayed bomblet count does not mean the clamp holds several bombs.
BOFORS, Howitzer, and the bomb clamp use the normal CAS firing workflow and require a fly-by rather than ordinary transport transit. [bold]An internal mount allows cabin servicing; it does not turn a CAS weapon into a landed turret.[/bold]
- [bold]Overview[/bold]: This system fires expensive, single-shot, high-impact guided rockets designed for taking out significant targets. - [bold]Firing Window[/bold]: Can [color=#FF0000]ONLY be used during Fly-by CAS runs[/color]. It cannot be fired while the dropship is in normal transit. - [bold]General Launcher Characteristics[/bold]: All missiles fired from this launcher have an inherent [color=#FFD700]3-tile inaccuracy[/color]. - [bold]Missile Options & Characteristics[/bold]:
This missile features a [color=#FF6347]large blast radius[/color]. Best used against large concentrations of enemies or widespread light targets. [color=#ADD8E6]Has a travel time of 3 seconds[/color]
This missile delivers its payload in a [color=#FF6347]small but highly concentrated blast radius[/color]. Designed for precision strikes against durable single targets. [color=#ADD8E6]Has a travel time of 2 seconds[/color]
This missile has a [color=#FF6347]large blast radius[/color] and creates an intense fire in a [color=#FFA500]7x7 area[/color] upon impact. Its primary use is for extreme area denial. [color=#ADD8E6]Has a travel time of 6 seconds[/color]
[bold]LAU-229 Rocket Pod[/bold]: Uses Mini-Mike ammunition packs, not the LAU-444's single guided missiles. Check the launcher name before printing ammunition. - [bold]Standard[/bold]: Explosive minirockets. - [bold]Incendiary[/bold]: Adds fire to the impact. - [bold]HEAT[/bold]: Anti-armor explosive payload. - [bold]Pressure / Thermobaric[/bold]: Pulls nearby targets toward the impact. - [bold]Flare[/bold]: Illuminates the impact area. - [bold]White-phosphorus smoke[/bold]: Creates a smoke screen and burning phosphorus. Smoke is not harmless cover. - [bold]Cluster Incendiary[/bold]: Releases six dispersed minirockets per trigger. - [bold]Weedkiller[/bold]: Delivers weedkiller over the impact area. Payloads differ in charge consumption, dispersion, and effects. Read the selected ammunition and remaining triggers instead of assuming every pack fires the same way.
### B. Engine Attachments These modules are fitted to dedicated engine attachment points to enhance dropship performance.
[color=#ADD8E6]Reduces overall travel time[/color] AND [color=#ADD8E6]increases available fly-by time by 25%[/color]. Excellent for rapid response, quicker transport cycles, and extended CAS presence.
[color=#ADD8E6]Significantly reduces dropship refuel time by 50%[/color], decreasing downtime at The Almayer or LZ. - [bold]Stacking Note[/bold]: Both engine attachments can be equipped simultaneously, and their effects stack, but with diminishing returns. The Pilot skill bonus also stacks with the Cooling System.
### C. Internal Utility Modules Dropships feature [bold]3 utility point[/bold], located inside the dropship near the rear. These mounts can be fitted with specialized modules to enhance the dropship's support capabilities. Currently, two primary utility modules are available:
- When this module is installed, the dropship gains the ability to [color=#ADD8E6]retrieve items or corpses that have been sent up from the ground via a fulton[/color]. The Pilot has to use their console to recover the fultonned items
- Equipping this module allows the dropship to [color=#00FF00]recover critically wounded or downed personnel on medevac stretcher directly from the battlefield[/color]. - To recover personnel with the medevac system, the pilot must first select the medevac system from the weapons console and has to manually interact with the medevac to activate it. The medevac system also has a 20 second cooldown - [bold][color=#FF0000]Vital for casualty evacuation. Remember to tend to the recovered personnel and inform medical on their status, do not leave them unattended after landing at the Almayer.[/color][/bold]
### D. Acquiring Armaments & Attachments (Dropship Fabricator) All weapon systems, their respective ammunition, and engine attachments are not freely available. They must be acquired through a Dropship Part Fabricator found above the landing pads
uses a system of [color=#FFFF00]"Dropship Points"[/color] to print these items. - [bold]Replenishing Dropship Points[/bold]: There are two primary ways to obtain or replenish these crucial dropship points:
1. [bold]Passive Regeneration[/bold]: Dropship points regenerate passively over time, but at a [color=#FFA500]very slow rate[/color] (approximately 1 point every 3 seconds). This method is often insufficient for rapid re-arming during active operations.
2. [bold]Command Intervention[/bold]: [color=#FFD700]The most effective and timely way to replenish spent dropship points is through Command intervention.[/color] Command staff can spend [color=#00FF00]"Intel Points"[/color] to purchase dropship points, which are then credited to the dropship systems for immediate fabrication of armaments and attachments.
- Check each item's point cost before printing. Running out of points prevents further fabrication until the balance is replenished.
## A. Accessing & Understanding the CAS Interface
Every aspect of a CAS run is controlled via the [bold]Weapons Controls Console[/bold]. - [bold]Dual Monitors:[/bold] Once the console is open, you will see two monitors. Both monitors can display the same selection of windows and operate independently, allowing you to have two different informational or control windows open simultaneously (Target on one, Cams on the other) - [bold]Available Buttons:[/bold] The primary windows accessible on these monitors are: [bold]Equip[/bold], [bold]Target[/bold], and [bold]Cams[/bold].
### B. Navigating the Weapon Control Buttons 1. [bold]The "Equip"[/bold] - Provides a detailed overview of the dropship's current loadout. - It shows what kind of weapon systems are attached to the dropship's weapon slots and displays the type and remaining quantity of ammunition for each installed weapon.
2. [bold]The "Cams"[/bold] - Provides a camera view centered on the selected target and its immediate surroundings. - When this window is active, it will display the visual feed from the area around the target currently selected. [bold]Camera Control[/bold]: - Located [italic]between the two main monitor windows[/italic], you will find four directional arrows. - Using these arrows allows you to [color=#ADD8E6]slightly move the camera view around[/color] the selected target point. You can use the button in the center to reset the camera back to the target. - [color=#FFD700][bold]Important Note[/bold][/color]: Selecting a different camera subject does not change the strike target, but the directional arrows change the console's shared offset. Direct CAS strikes land at the selected strike target plus that offset. Check the targeting preview and reset the offset when you no longer need it.
3. [bold]The "Target"[/bold] - This is your primary interface for selecting targets and firing the dropship's weapon systems. [bold]Firing Sequence - Step-by-Step:[/bold] - [color=#FFA500][bold]Select Target[/bold][/color]: You must choose a target. On the right side of the "Target" window, a list of available targets will be displayed. These targets are typically those designated by ground teams using [color=#FF0000]Laser Designators[/color] or [color=#00FF00]Signal Flares[/color]. Click on the desired target to select it. - [color=#FFA500][bold]Select "Strike"[/bold][/color]: Once a target is selected, press the "Strike" button within the window. - [color=#FFA500][bold]Select "Weapon"[/bold][/color]: This will bring up a list showing all equipped weapon systems. - [color=#FFA500][bold]Choose Your Weapon[/bold][/color]: Select the specific weapon system you intend to fire at the chosen target. - [bold]Check the preview and payload settings[/bold]: With a weapon and valid target selected, the strike/weapon view can display the target camera with an overlay. Check the next burst, remaining bursts, and any laser-pattern or airburst-height setting. - [color=#FF0000][bold]Select "Fire"[/bold][/color]: Confirm your selections by pressing the "Fire" button. - [bold]If the sequence was performed correctly, you should hear the distinct sound of the selected weapon firing.[/bold]
[bold]Weapon Cooldowns & Rapid Fire:[/bold] - Individual weapons have a [italic]short internal cooldown[/italic] before they can be fired again. - However, there is [bold]no hard delay between firing -different- guns[/bold]. This means once one weapon has fired (example GAU-21), you can immediately repeat the "Strike" -> "Weapon" (select a different GAU-21 or another weapon) -> "Fire" sequence to unleash another salvo with a different weapon system very quickly. This allows for potent combined-arms attacks.
### C. Reading Targeting Previews
- [bold]Yellow outlines[/bold] show the estimated payload footprint. For a Rapidfire battery, the five separate outlines show its five impact areas. - [bold]Orange outlines[/bold] show the dispersion envelope around the target. They are not a guarantee that every tile inside the outline will be damaged. - Blast previews use an unobstructed estimate. Walls, overhead cover, penetration, blast resistance, and tile snapping affect actual impacts. Fire footprints can contain gaps. - A camera can observe a different target from the selected strike target. [bold]Changing camera subjects alone does not select a new strike target.[/bold] - The shared directional-arrow [bold]offset does affect direct CAS aim[/bold]: a direct strike uses the selected target plus that offset. Reset it with the center button. During a fire mission, the mission's vector and per-weapon step offsets control the pass.
### D. Fire Missions
Open [bold]Fire Mission[/bold] to create and name a mission, then use its editor to select weapons and assign offsets at the available timing steps. A blank offset means that weapon will not fire at that step. Use weapon-page buttons to reach internal mounts or additional guns.
Choose the mission from the strike menu, select a designated target, choose the strike vector, and fire. The mission advances along that vector and releases the scheduled weapons at their steps. Check the ammunition totals before starting; mixed GAU belts advance one crate per scheduled burst. Weapons on [bold]internal mounts[/bold] (shown as INT, such as the bomb clamp or an internal BOFORS or Howitzer) can be scheduled like any external weapon. Dedicated gunnery-only and direct-fire-only guns, such as the Mohawk M90, cannot be added to a fire mission. Fire missions skip the danger close confirmation, and their weapons do not roll jams.
### E. Mohawk 90mm Chin Turret
The fixed triple-feed twin 90mm M90 chin gun fires at approximately [bold]three shells per second[/bold] with explosive ammunition, or [bold]fifteen rounds per second (900 RPM)[/bold] with Squall kinetic ammunition. Landed acquisition has a [bold]225-degree arc[/bold] and a [bold]20-tile range measured from the chin mount[/bold]; the gun rotates at sixty degrees per second and must align before firing physical shells. Unmanned close defense scans all directions within eight tiles and auto-fires valid hostiles. During [bold]airborne flight (flybys and transit)[/bold], the gunner selects a signal flare and rains delayed impacts within ten tiles of it; airborne AI scanning requires gunner approval for each target. Takeoff and tactical hover do not support flare bombardment. Sustained HEAP fire heats the barrels; see [bold]Barrel heat[/bold] below.
[bold]Startup and hardpoint faults[/bold]: Before using the M90, ground the ship and use a [bold]screwdriver[/bold] on the actual chin hardpoint to calibrate it, then a [bold]multitool[/bold] to program your faction identification. A recognized faction is required; ship faction alone does not complete setup. The console shows whether setup is ready. These steps persist, including through a rebuild. A multitool can reprogram an already calibrated gun. Opening the Mohawk's dedicated gunnery console for the first time starts a ship-wide boot sequence: initialization, then installed-weapon self tests, with audible boot, ready and fault tones at the consoles. Weapon fire is blocked during boot. Each installed weapon hardpoint has a [bold]10% chance[/bold] (server-configurable) of a self-test fault. The console lists each faulted hardpoint with its [bold]fault reason[/bold] (gyro desync, feed sensor error, circuit short, IFF handshake failure, servo stall or coolant pressure), and examining the hardpoint shows the same reason. Go to each physical hardpoint and use a [bold]multitool[/bold] to reset it; this requires [bold]Pilot skill 2 or Engineering skill 1[/bold]. Only the faulted weapon is disabled. Reopening a console or using another console does not reroll the test. Interrupted setup and resets do not complete. [bold]Post-landing diagnostics[/bold]: after the fire-control system has booted, every completed landing re-runs a short diagnostic. Each hardpoint rolls a landing fault chance that starts at 2% and rises 1% per landing since its last repair, multiplied by +5% for every firing engagement from that hardpoint since its last repair, tripled after a crash landing, and capped at 75%. Existing faults are kept. Repairing a hardpoint resets its landing and use counters. Admins can tune all of these with the [bold]cmu.dropship.*[/bold] CVars: boot_fault_chance, landing_reboot, landing_fault_chance, landing_fault_step, fault_use_multiplier, crash_fault_multiplier and fault_max_chance.
[bold]90mm ammunition and loading[/bold]: Squall crates contain [bold]1200 rounds[/bold]; each explosive crate contains [bold]400 rounds[/bold]. Every groundside shot or airborne impact consumes [bold]one round[/bold]. Obtain them from the dropship fabricator's [bold]Ammo[/bold] category. The mount accepts [bold]three physical crates[/bold]. [bold]Feed 3 is reserved for PGU-410 Squall[/bold]; feeds 1 and 2 are dealer's choice and take any M90 crate, for up to 3600 rounds with three Squall crates. Use a powerloader to install each crate: Squall fills feed 3 first, everything else fills feeds 1 then 2. Non-Squall crates are rejected once feeds 1 and 2 are full, with a message explaining the restriction. Unload a crate before replacing it. Activating the mount with a powerloader unloads feed 1, then feed 2, then feed 3. These are M90-only crates, not GAU-21 ammunition; the GAU mixed-belt carrier is not compatible. The weapon itself remains permanently mounted. In the gunnery console, press [bold]Feed 1[/bold], [bold]Feed 2[/bold] or [bold]Feed 3[/bold] to select a feed. [bold]Feed mode: selected[/bold] uses that crate until empty, then automatically uses another loaded feed. Toggle [bold]Feed mode: alternate each shell[/bold] to cycle the loaded crates after every consumed round; missing, empty and flight-incompatible feeds are skipped. [bold]Low ammunition[/bold]: when any loaded crate drops below [bold]25%[/bold] of a full crate, the console shows an orange [bold]LOW AMMO[/bold] line listing each low feed and its percentage, and the gunner gets a warning popup and buzzer once per crate. Refilling or swapping the crate re-arms the warning. Selecting a numbered feed returns to selected-feed mode. The console shows each crate's name and remaining rounds; blocked shots do not consume ammo or advance the feed. - [bold]PGU-410 'Squall' kinetic[/bold] (750 fabricator points): usable [bold]groundside, in transit, and during flybys[/bold], 1200 rounds of budget rapid-fire suppression at fifteen rounds per second (900 RPM). Each round deals 20 piercing damage with 30 armor piercing and GAU-style non-explosive impacts. No ground dispersion or overhead penetration. Ground projectiles terminate at your cursor aimpoint [bold]inside the twenty-tile circle[/bold]; manual shots outside the circle continue until collision. Both still obey traverse, slew and IFF checks. They pass through dead bodies; living targets and solid obstructions can intercept them. Squall never ejects casings. - [bold]PGU-420 HEAP[/bold] (3000 fabricator points): precision general-purpose armor piercing; 145 piercing + 20 heat direct damage, 60 armor piercing, and up to three levels of aerial cover penetration. Airborne impacts disperse up to two tiles. [bold]Usable groundside[/bold], but every HEAP shell adds far more barrel heat than Squall. - [bold]PGU-425 'Gale' scatter[/bold] (3000 points): wide, low-damage suppression; 50 piercing + 10 heat and 10 armor piercing. Airborne impacts disperse up to five tiles. No overhead penetration. - [bold]PGU-430 'Ember' incendiary[/bold] (3000 points): 70 piercing + 60 heat and 15 armor piercing. Airborne impacts create burning tiles and disperse up to three tiles. No overhead penetration. - [bold]PGU-440 'Tempest' devastator[/bold] (6000 points): expensive high-damage saturation; 220 piercing + 80 heat and 40 armor piercing, with a wider high-yield explosive impact (100 total intensity, slope 3, peak 12). Airborne impacts disperse up to six tiles. Up to one level of aerial cover penetration. Requires six tiles of friendly clearance around the intended impact. [bold]PGU-410 Squall and PGU-420 HEAP are usable groundside; Gale, Ember and Tempest are airborne-only (flybys and transit).[/bold] The console rejects selecting an incompatible feed, and neither manual fire nor AI can bypass this restriction. If an incompatible feed is left selected after a flight-mode change or feed alternation, select a compatible crate to resume. Blocked shots consume no rounds. Explosive airborne dispersion can miss the intended entity; fire and explosions can still harm nearby troops. IFF is not blanket immunity to blast or fire. Overhead-penetration ratings describe aerial CAS.
[bold]Barrel heat[/bold]: The console shows a [bold]BARREL HEAT[/bold] bar. Each HEAP shell adds 8 heat; each Squall round adds 0.6. The barrels cool 8 heat per second. At 100 heat the M90 [bold]overheats[/bold]: firing locks out, held fire and pending shots are cancelled, and the gunner is warned. Fire resumes once heat falls to 40. Squall can fire almost indefinitely; sustained HEAP fire overheats in a few seconds, so fire HEAP in short bursts.
[bold]Manual aiming[/bold]: 1. Buckle into the Mohawk's gunnery seat and open the dedicated gunnery console. 2. Press [bold]Take turret control[/bold]. This replaces automatic observation with manual aiming; taking control alone does not authorize fire. 3. [bold]Move the mouse inside the left camera[/bold] to slew without firing. [bold]Hold left click[/bold] to fire continuously while following your cursor at the loaded round's fire rate. Release the button to stop; moving outside the camera, clearing tracking, panning, closing the console or losing control stops held fire. The gun waits for alignment. Explosive rounds eject a spent casing with randomized throw direction, distance, speed and spin beneath the chin mount. These casings disappear after ten seconds; Squall produces none. 4. The overlay shows the forward arc, range, and aim marker. Red indicates an out-of-range/out-of-arc aimpoint or confirmed tracked engagement; green indicates an aimpoint inside the arc and range. It does not guarantee an unobstructed shot. 5. Use [bold]WASD[/bold] to move the camera and slew the gun, or the [bold]directional arrows[/bold] to pan two tiles per press. Pan forward to see targets at the full twenty-tile acquisition range, or sideways to inspect the arc. The center button recenters on the mount or selected flare. Camera centers stay inside the turret's arc and range. Groundside, walls stop the camera, tracking and AI acquisition in Normal and Night optics; airborne cameras and Thermal optics ignore walls. Smoke from WP rockets hides targets from Normal and Night optics; Thermal sees through it. Panning clears tracking and fire authorization. 6. Press [bold]AR mode[/bold] to hide the console and use the main view as the gun camera, with the firing arc/radius drawn in the world. WASD pans, moving the cursor aims, and held left click fires. AR and the embedded gun camera follow the same wall rules as the camera above. The [bold]Return to gun panel[/bold] button restores the console without releasing control. Leaving the seat, losing turret control or closing the console exits AR and restores your normal camera. 7. The [bold]IFF ENABLED[/bold] button toggles friendly protection. With IFF disabled, manual fire can pass through friendlies and airborne impacts can harm them; AI still acquires faction hostiles. Changing IFF clears existing target approvals. Disabling IFF does not bypass setup, cover, traverse or boot faults. [bold]AI IFF lock[/bold]: while groundside AI free fire is running unmanned, IFF is [bold]forced on[/bold] regardless of the toggle and the button reads [bold]IFF LOCKED ON - AI FREE FIRE[/bold]. The lock releases to your toggle only when the gun is in [bold]self defense[/bold] (a live hostile within the eight-tile close-defense ring) or [bold]overwhelmed[/bold] (four or more live hostiles within its scan range); the button shows which. The lock returns once the threat clears. Manual control and airborne fire always use your toggle. 8. The [bold]OPTICS[/bold] button cycles the gun camera through [bold]Normal[/bold], [bold]Night[/bold] (green-tinted light amplification that ignores darkness) and [bold]Thermal[/bold] (orange-tinted, ignores darkness and lets the camera and AR view see through walls, even groundside). Thermal is a viewing aid only: walls still block shots and line-of-fire checks. 9. The console's [bold]PLT / GNR[/bold] line is a shared flare list. The flare the pilot selected for CAS is tagged [bold]PLT[/bold] and the flare the gunner locked or is free-firing on is tagged [bold]GNR[/bold] in every weapons console's target list on the same ship.
[bold]Tracking a target[/bold]: 1. While in manual control, press [bold]Mark target[/bold], then click a visible entity in the left camera view. PGU-410 can mark any living entity, including critically wounded entities; explosive ammunition can mark any entity, including objects and corpses. The mark button arms the next click; it does not select a target by itself. Alternatively press [bold]Acquire priority target[/bold] to select a visible living IFF hostile automatically. Marking a friendly does not bypass friendly-fire safety. 2. The camera follows the target and displays its range. Marking alone does [bold]not[/bold] fire. 3. Press the center-column [bold]Authorize fire (30 seconds)[/bold] button to authorize repeated fire at that specific entity. The button is always shown during manual control, but is disabled until a valid target is marked or while authorization is active. Moving the cursor while tracking does not replace the marked target. 4. Press [bold]Stop / clear tracking[/bold] to stop tracked engagement and return to manual aiming. Clicking the left camera to fire manually also clears tracking.
Losing groundside sight, range, or the forward firing arc pauses engagement without extending the thirty-second authorization. The camera stops following an invisible target. Reacquiring the same entity before expiry resumes engagement; after expiry, confirm again. Death clears a Squall mark; explosive ammunition can retain corpse marks. Transparent windows do not prevent groundside acquisition, but opaque walls do. Living friendlies in the bullet's path or near its intended impact block groundside shots; dead bodies do not block bullets. Airborne shots check friendly clearance near the dispersed impact at launch and again when it lands. Empty feeds stop confirmed engagement when no usable rounds remain. Closing the console, leaving the seat, or changing between groundside and flyby control releases control and clears authorization.
[bold]Flare-assisted gunnery[/bold]: 1. During an [bold]active CAS flyby or transit flight[/bold], take control from the gunnery seat, open [bold]TARGET[/bold] on the right monitor, and select an active signal flare from the designation list. Flare targeting works during flybys and transit; it is unavailable while landed or tactically hovering. Laser designations and other beacon types are not flare anchors. 2. The left camera recenters on the flare on its ground map. A cyan ring marks a [bold]ten-tile engagement radius[/bold]. Selecting a new flare warns every player within that radius with an on-screen warning and a chat message. Hold left click and move the mouse to bombard within that ring, or mark and authorize a target. Each shot consumes one round at approximately three shots per second for explosive shells or ten for Squall, and creates an impact after a randomized [bold]one-to-two-second travel delay[/bold]; no physical projectile flies from the dropship. Impacts use the selected ammunition's damage, explosion, fire and cover-penetration properties; Squall remains non-explosive. The landed twenty-tile arc does not apply to flyby bombardment. 3. Mark a hostile within the ring, or press [bold]Acquire priority target[/bold], then [bold]Authorize fire[/bold] to track that entity. This never blindly bombards the flare itself or grants blanket authorization for new targets. 4. Use [bold]Clear flare / recenter[/bold] to deselect the flare and stop airborne shots. Selecting or clearing a flare cancels the previous mark, held trigger and authorization. Actual dispersed impacts must remain within the ten-tile circle and pass cover and friendly checks. An invalid/deleted flare or the end of the flyby prevents new shots. Released shells already in flight keep their fixed impact coordinates; authorization and cursor movement do not steer them.
[bold]Automatic observation and close defense[/bold]: The seated gunner can press [bold]Enable AI free fire scanning[/bold] to release manual control and enable continuous acquisition. Groundside, it uses the full twenty-tile, 225-degree arc, with all-direction close defense within eight tiles. The left gun camera follows the AI lock and marks it yellow while waiting. Press [bold]APPROVE AI TARGET[/bold] to authorize that specific target, or revoke its approval with the same button. [bold]While airborne, every newly selected target requires new approval.[/bold] Groundside, the AI engages valid targets without approval. Approval ends when the target changes, becomes critical or invalid, or you take manual control. During a CAS flyby, the AI scans [bold]all active signal flares[/bold] and locks onto one containing a valid hostile, then engages within its ten-tile circle using delayed single-round impacts. No manual flare selection is required. It retains its target until critical or invalid, then searches all flares again. Switching to a new flare issues the same nearby warning as a manual lock; repeated warnings for one flare are suppressed for thirty seconds. Approved fire still respects slew alignment, cooldown, cover and enabled IFF protection. No hostile or no approval means no shots. AI free fire and ordinary unmanned ground defense automatically select among the [bold]actually loaded feeds[/bold]. Ground defense selects ground-compatible Squall or HEAP. Airborne selection estimates time to defeat the target using remaining health and armor, favors wider explosive/fire payloads against nearby groups, and rejects ammunition that cannot penetrate cover or meet friendly clearance. A safe narrower feed can replace an unsafe explosive feed. With matching loaded ammunition it alternates boxes; with different payloads it uses the best selected feed. It cannot create ammunition or load a missing crate. Taking manual control stops automatic feed/mode selection so your manual choices remain authoritative. AI scanning [bold]only disables when you press its button[/bold]. There is no expiry timer. Manual control, unsupported flight modes and damage pause it without disabling it. Closing the console or leaving the seat does not disable an approved AI engagement. A [bold]five-minute cooldown begins when the button disables scanning[/bold]. Ordinary eight-tile close-defense scanning resumes and still auto-fires groundside. Changing priority or feed settings requires the gunnery seat.
[bold]Damage and rebuilding[/bold]: The exposed chin mount has [bold]2000 HP[/bold]. Bullets and tier-two-or-higher xeno melee attacks can damage it; tier-one xeno melee cannot. At zero integrity it remains installed but disables all firing modes, releases the operator and clears target approval without disabling the AI scanning toggle. Ordinary healing cannot bypass the rebuild requirement. The console displays integrity and the disabled state; examine the actual chin mount to see the next repair step. Ground the dropship, then have someone with at least [bold]engineer skill 1[/bold] perform these steps on the mount in order: 1. Use a [bold]wrench[/bold] to strip the damaged mechanism. 2. Install [bold]90mm repair parts[/bold] from the dropship fabricator's Equipment category for [bold]1500 points[/bold]. One box is consumed only on successful installation. 3. Add [bold]ten lengths of cable[/bold], consumed on completion. 4. Weld the housing with a [bold]lit blowtorch[/bold] and five units of welding fuel. Use welding eye protection. 5. Use a [bold]screwdriver[/bold] to calibrate and close the mechanism. Moving away, changing or dropping the held item, or taking damage interrupts the current action without consuming its parts or cable; completed stages persist. The final calibration restores all 2000 HP but does not reset the AI free-fire cooldown. Ammunition stays in its feeds.
Press [bold]Priority: nearest[/bold] to switch to [bold]Priority: highest health[/bold], or press again to return. Highest health means greatest remaining health before death, not damage already taken; distance breaks equal-health ties. Once automatic fire selects a target, it retains that target until it becomes [bold]critical[/bold] or is no longer visible, hostile or in range. Damage alone does not make it switch to a healthier enemy. Critical and dead targets are excluded from AI acquisition. This setting controls unmanned observation and Acquire priority target. Neither observation nor acquisition alone authorizes ordinary fire.
[bold]Release / close defense[/bold], closing the console, or leaving the seat clears manual authorization. While unmanned and landed with PGU-410 selected, the turret scans visible IFF hostiles within eight tiles of the chin mount in any direction and auto-fires without requiring manual approval. Close threats take precedence over distant observation targets; the selected priority ranks threats within that radius. This scan never overrides an active manual operator. Slew alignment, kinetic firing cooldown, and enabled friendly-fire checks still apply. Airborne AI scanning continues to require gunner target approval before firing.
### F. Pre-flight and Ground Crew Checklist
Examine any weapon or utility hardpoint to read its [bold]ground crew checklist[/bold]: weapon installed, ammunition loaded and compatible, fault status with the fault reason, and the hardpoint's wear (firing engagements and landings since its last repair), its current landing fault chance and its jam chance. The weapons console shows a [bold]LOADOUT[/bold] summary (every hardpoint with its location tag, such as FWD, WING or INT, weapon and remaining ammunition) and a [bold]PREFLIGHT[/bold] line listing anything that will stop a strike: empty mounts, missing ammunition, faulted hardpoints or a running boot.
### G. Weapon Jams
Every time a CAS weapon fires (except as part of a fire mission), it can [bold]jam[/bold]. The base chance is 2% (server-configurable), raised by the same wear multiplier as landing faults and capped by the same limit. A jam plays a stoppage sound, warns the shooter and faults the hardpoint with a reason such as a feed tray jam or a double-feed stoppage. A jammed hardpoint cannot fire until someone with [bold]Pilot skill 2 or Engineering skill 1[/bold] uses a [bold]multitool[/bold] on it. Repairs reset its wear.
### H. Danger Close
When a console-fired strike would land within [bold]five tiles of a living friendly[/bold], the first shot is held and the gunner gets a [bold]DANGER CLOSE[/bold] warning with a warning tone. Fire again at the same spot within five seconds to confirm. Strikes near a target covered by an accepted or cleared-hot RTO request skip the warning, because the ground commander has already accepted the risk. Every warning and confirmation is admin-logged.
### I. RTO Close Air Support Requests
Radio Telephone Operators wearing an AN/PRC radio pack can file a [bold]CAS request[/bold] (a simplified 9-line) on any mark within [bold]45 tiles[/bold]. [bold]CAS uplink[/bold]: the radio pack grants a [bold]CAS uplink[/bold] action that opens the request window. It lists every friendly flare, laser spot and radio mark in range with distance, [bold]DANGER CLOSE[/bold] and [bold]LASER[/bold] tags, plus a [bold]NO FLARE: nearest hostile[/bold] entry. Picking a mark shows a live preview of exactly what will be transmitted: mark type, target, grid, hostiles, friendlies, distance and warnings. Choose the [bold]weapon system[/bold] (any, guns, GAU-21, BOFORS, howitzer, rockets, missiles, bombs, lasers or M90 chin gun) and the [bold]desired effect[/bold] (high explosive, armor piercing, incendiary, fragmentation, smoke or illumination), add optional remarks, and press [bold]Transmit request[/bold]. The window also lists your open requests with [bold]Cleared hot[/bold] and [bold]Abort[/bold] buttons. [bold]No-flare calls[/bold]: choosing the nearest-hostile entry drops a short-lived [bold]radio mark[/bold] on the closest living hostile within 45 tiles, which the aircrew can target and view like a flare. [bold]Laser designation[/bold]: a strike landing within two tiles of a spot lased by an RTO wearing a radio pack is [bold]25% more accurate[/bold] (reduced spread and dispersion). You can still right-click a signal flare or laser mark (or yourself, to use the nearest friendly mark) and open [bold]Request CAS[/bold] for a quick call. The request records the callsign, target mark, grid location and area, a description of the hostiles near the target, the nearest friendlies, and whether the strike would be danger close. It is announced on the faction's JTAC radio channel. Every weapons console of that faction lists open requests in its [bold]CAS REQUESTS[/bold] panel: 1. [bold]Accept[/bold] takes the job, selects its mark as the console's target and radios the RTO. 2. The RTO then uses [bold]Request CAS → Clear hot[/bold] on themselves to authorize the strike, or [bold]Abort[/bold] to cancel it. 3. [bold]Deny[/bold] declines the request. 4. After accepting, the pilot picks [bold]AUTO[/bold] or [bold]MANUAL[/bold] carry-out on the request card. With no choice within [bold]12 seconds[/bold], the request defaults to AUTO. AUTO has the fire control computer fire up to three volleys from every matching onboard weapon (or any weapon if none match) at the mark when the weapons can fire; danger-close requests still wait for the RTO's clear hot. The M90 chin gun and flare launchers never fire automatically. MANUAL leaves the strike to the crew. 5. After the strike, press [bold]Rounds complete[/bold] (AUTO completes itself after its volleys). The aircraft radios a battle damage assessment (hostiles down and still standing near the mark). Each mark can carry one open request, and each faction can have six open at once. Requests expire after fifteen minutes or when their mark disappears.
### J. Special Rocket Fallout
- [bold]Weedkiller[/bold]: leaves a treated zone (three-tile radius, about five minutes) where weeds cannot spread or be planted. - [bold]White phosphorus smoke[/bold]: leaves a smoke screen (three-tile radius, about twenty seconds). Targets inside it cannot be laser-designated, and M90 Normal and Night optics cannot track or acquire them. Thermal optics see through the smoke. - [bold]Flare[/bold]: leaves a burning flare for about sixty seconds that is itself a targetable CAS mark (RKT). - [bold]Thermobaric[/bold] (Mini-Mike and BLU-176): the overpressure heavily damages resin structures within two tiles. - [bold]HEAT[/bold]: the shaped-charge jet deals bonus damage to vehicles and heavily armored targets at the impact.
### K. Admin Tools
Admins have [bold]CAS (Admin)[/bold] verbs. On a hardpoint: clear fault, force fault, refill ammunition and (on the M90) restore the chin gun to full working order. On a weapons console: skip the boot sequence, force a landing reboot, refill every hardpoint and clear every fault. All CAS weapon fire, fire missions, ammunition loads, setting changes, jams, overheats, requests and admin actions are written to the admin logs.
### L. Gameplay Troubleshooting
- [bold]Weapon missing from the list[/bold]: Check whether it is installed on a compatible point, then browse the weapon pages. A dedicated direct-fire-only weapon is not a normal CAS selection. - [bold]Cannot load[/bold]: Match the ammunition to the weapon, clear the occupied ammunition slot, and use the correct method: powerloader for heavy packs, both hands free for individual hand-loaded rounds. - [bold]Cannot fire[/bold]: Read the popup. Check flight mode, pilot skill, cooldown, loaded ammunition, and whether a fire mission is already active. Most CAS weapons cannot fire while landed. - [bold]Target disappeared[/bold]: Have the ground player designate again, then reselect the target. - [bold]Strike rejected under cover[/bold]: Select ammunition with suitable overhead penetration. Dispersion can move an impact beneath protected cover even when the central target is valid. - [bold]Weapon jammed or faulted[/bold]: Examine the hardpoint for its fault reason, then multitool it (Pilot 2 or Engineering 1). - [bold]First shot did nothing and DANGER CLOSE appeared[/bold]: Friendlies are within five tiles. Fire again within five seconds to confirm, or pick another target. - [bold]M90 stopped firing with HEAP[/bold]: The barrels overheated. Wait until heat falls to 40, or switch to Squall. - [bold]Belt still has rounds but will not fire[/bold]: Every remaining crate may contain fewer than forty rounds. Leftover rounds from different crates are not combined into a burst. - [bold]Pattern/height button missing[/bold]: Pattern selection requires a Rapidfire laser battery; height selection requires a BOFORS Airburst magazine. - [bold]Turret will not track[/bold]: Take control from the gunnery seat with ammunition appropriate to the flight mode. Squall marks require a living entity inside the forward arc and range; explosive marks require an entity inside the selected flyby flare circle. Targets inside WP smoke cannot be tracked with Normal or Night optics.
### M. Practical Gameplay Tips
- [bold]Use both monitors[/bold]: Keep "Target" open for firing and "Cams" or "Equip" open for observation or ammunition checks. - [bold]Account for travel time[/bold]: The target can move between release and impact. Fast laser strikes and slower missiles or bombs require different lead distances. - [bold]Monitor ammunition[/bold]: Check the loaded payload and full bursts remaining before starting a mission. - [bold]Switch weapons during cooldowns[/bold]: Another ready weapon can fire while the first weapon cools down. - [bold]Reset offsets when changing tasks[/bold]: A forgotten direct-fire offset shifts subsequent strikes away from their designation. - [bold]Check the actual aimpoint[/bold]: Ordinary CAS uses the selected strike target plus the console offset, not an arbitrary camera subject. The manually controlled Mohawk chin turret instead uses your click in its left camera view. - [bold]Allow room for scatter and fire[/bold]: CAS explosions and burning tiles can damage nearby allies. The preview is an estimate, not a friendly-fire barrier. - [bold]Match the payload to the job[/bold]: Use precision or AP payloads for focused targets, fragmentation for exposed groups, and incendiaries for persistent area denial.
